rationale: The nightly job has no explicit timeout, so it falls back to the default 360-minute job limit and can consume a long runner window if a step hangs. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the measured experiment example batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, which added timeout-minutes: 5 to a job and retained all successes while reducing elapsed time. The change is minimal: only timeout-minutes: 5 is added to the job. All existing steps (checkout, Node setup with npm cache, install, tests, build, deploy) and the existing concurrency cancel-in-progress, path filters, and permissions are preserved, so build/test coverage and the deploy step are unchanged. No permissions are weakened, no new secrets or network access are added, and no publishing/deployment operation is introduced.
